title: Tunable nonlinear electromechanics at the zero-point motion scale
summary: Nonlinearity at the scale of zero-point motion opens new possibilities for the control and readout of nanomechanical systems, but achieving this remains a formidable challenge. Here we demonstrate that ultrastrong coupling (USC) between a nanotube mechanical oscillator and a double-quantum-dot electronic two-level system enables a mechanical Kerr (Duffing) nonlinearity at the zero-point motion scale.
